description: Sensitivity variant of bvi-v0. A crossing counts as PASS on ANY positive accessibility evidence - markings, a lowered kerb, an island, a pedestrian signal - not only tactile paving or acoustic signals. Use to test whether the decidability gap is an artefact of a strict crossing rule. See docs/routing-feasibility.md section 5.1.

sidewalk.comment: Missing sidewalk evidence is unresolved, not evidence of physical absence. Separately mapped sidewalks do not establish an additional passing centreline geometry.

pedestrianWays.comment: Dedicated pedestrian infrastructure is PASS unless something contradicts it.

crossing.comment: A crossing is the decision point that matters most for a blind pedestrian. PASS needs a positive accessibility signal; an explicit negative blocks; silence is UNKNOWN.

steps.comment: Steps primary rule uses handrail OR tactile evidence; explicit blockers dominate.

surface.comment: Surfaces that defeat a long cane or a guide dog. `degrade` does not block but is reported separately as a quality caveat.

minUsableComponentKmComment: A declared fragmentation convention, not proof of trip usefulness. Eligible metrics threshold eligible component mass; legacy graph metrics threshold total admitted mass.
